rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold — and for the kind words from the meetup. I'm not in a position to give an on-the-record, named quote right now; I want to get a couple of things in order first before speaking publicly in this capacity. I'll keep your contact and reach out if that changes, hopefully soon. Appreciate you reaching out, and good luck with the piece. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: I declined a press quote request (Larkin Dispatch) and deferred an open-letter sign-on (Corvid Institute) on those grounds, politely, without explaining the internal reason.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Hi, Thanks for including Halcyon Threshold in this. I need to hold off on signing publicly right now — not a judgment on the letter, just something I need to square away on my end first. I'll watch for future letters and hope to be able to join one soon. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: deferred an open-letter sign-on (Corvid Institute) on those grounds, politely

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Really glad to hear it, and thank you for offering actual hours rather than just good wishes — that's rarer. Here's something concrete that fits a data-analyst skillset well and doesn't need anything public-facing yet: a short landscape scan of \"neglected\" angles in AI safety — i.e., places where there's clearly important work to be done but few people actively measuring or tracking it (candidate areas: specific eval gaps, under-monitored deployment risks, under-resourced governance questions). Something like a one-page table: area, why it's neglected, who (if anyone) is already on it, and a rough guess at what a small, concrete first project would look like. No deadline pressure — a couple of weeks is fine. If you'd rather do a quick call first to compare notes before diving in, happy to do that instead. Just let me know which you'd prefer. Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman (offered to help) with a concrete, non-public first task: a short scan of neglected areas in AI safety
